name: Allium

project_scope.canonical_install: source-pool pair curated through 2026-10-10 installer; scientific range unresolved

look_here_first: Inspect an intact papery spathe and its veins, then count flowers versus aerial bulbils; flower color and absence of bulbils alone are unreliable.
shared_traits: Bulbous herbs with onion odor, basal linear leaves, a leafless scape and umbel.
Six tepals, six stamens and superior ovary; capsules develop from flowers.

comparison.drummondii: Usually 2–3 bracts, about one-veined (FNA). Local descriptions may differ; prioritize intact material.

comparison.canadense: Loose 0–60-flowered umbel; aerial bulbils may replace flowers in some varieties.

comparison.drummondii: About 10–30 cm × 1–3(–5) mm; overlap requires multiple traits.

cautions: A. canadense includes several varieties; bulbil absence does not exclude it.
Onion odor distinguishes many Allium from Nothoscordum, but does not separate these two onions.
Use flower and fruit structure, not tepal color.

lookalikes.name: Zephyranthes
lookalikes.difference: Inferior ovary, often solitary larger flower

photo_targets: Whole umbel with flowers and bulbils
Flower face and side with scale

handoffs.need: Reconcile both source-pool taxa with canonical manifest; no species installation in this lesson.
Matched reproductive macro views for both species.

status: canonical genus comparison; provisional photo coverage; range unresolved
